PAN AMERICAN AIRWAYS SYSTEM
Pacific-Alaska
FRANSPACIFIE DIVISION, TREASURE IStAND, SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA
February 19, 1945
OFFICE OF THE
DIVISION MANAGER
PERSONAL
Mr. and Mrs. H. M. Bixby
2 Normandy Road
Bronxville, New York
Dear Mr. and Mrs. Bixby:
As contemplated when I telegraphed you Saturday (Feb-
ruary 17), Catherine arrived in Vallejo that morning, completed
her "reporting-in" procedure, then came down to Hillsborough
that evening.
Damaris, Mother and I-and, cf course, Gretchen
and Alice--are hopeful that Catherine will want to stay with us
until she leaves.
She is & very comfortable house guest and
has already made deep inroads into the affections of Mother and
the children. Gretchen is distressed, however, that Catherine,
at her advanced age, is not long since married and settled dov n;
at least she deplored that fact in conversation with Catherine
at dinner Saturday evening.
To the extent Demaris's gas holds out, she plans to
show Catherine some of the local sights of interest. When I
get back from Seattle, we will organize a Chinese chow party
for Catherine and & few other young folks, at our favorite
restaurant in Chinatown.
I am letting Captain Ingalls and Bill Mullahey know
Catherine is here, and will notify them when she leaves. In
the meantime I will try, as far as it is consistent with Bix's
position in the Company, to prevail upon Naval Air Priorities
to send Catherine out by Clipper. On the basis of Jean Kingman's
experience, I am not very optimistic, however.
Sincerely.
Le C. Reynolds
properties.sfomuseum:description: Typewritten letter from L.C. “Tom” Reynolds to Harold and Debby Bixby, dated February 19, 1945, on Pan American Airways System stationery; marked “Personal”; includes description of arrival of Catherine (daughter Cat?) in Vallejo, California, and entertainment plans; attempt to send her out on the Clipper under Naval Air Priorities; mentions Captain Ingalls, Bill Mullahey, and Jean Kingman.
